text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Sri Lanka bought 50,000 tonnes of Australian soft wheat at about $169.75 a tonne, cost and freight, slated for January 13-22 shipment, and 50,000 tonnes Argentinian hard wheat at about $168.00 a tonne C and F, set for February 5-14, exporters said.
SOYBEAN AND SOYOIL SALES - USDA in its weekly export sales report said 10,000 tonnes of soyoil and 46,300 tonnes of soybeans were sold to China.

GRAIN AND OILSEED SALES - South Korea bought at leasst 230,500 tonnes of grains and oilseeds through tenders and private negotiations in December versus 231,500 tonnes in November, traders at commodities houses said.
WHEAT TENDERS - Pakistan will tender January 12 for 315,000 tonnes of Australian white milling wheat and U.S. soft white wheat. Shipment was slated for February 1-28.
- The Commodity Credit Corp said it seeks up to 30,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better hard red winter wheat for donation to Bosnia. Shipment is for January 25-February 20. Offers are due January 7.

WHEAT TENDERS - Yemen on January 7 will seek 200,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat flour for February-June shipment and 200,000 tonnes of new-crop U.S., Canadian or Australian soft white wheat for July-September, European traders said.

- Bangladesh seeks 100,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 wheat or Australian standard or better Canadian winter red/spring wheat for shipment by February 21, food ministry officials said. Offers are to be opened January 18 and results announced two to three days later.

BARLEY TENDER - Saudi Arabia was to tender next week for barley, Canadian grain trade sources said. European traders said last week they expected Saudi Arabia to seek about 500,000 tonnes of barley this week.

SOYBEAN OIL TENDER - The CCC is to tender for 10,370 tonnes of U.S. bulk crude degummed soybean oil for donation to Peru. Delivery was for February 3-18. Offers were requested by January 7. Successful offerers will be notified January 8.

MARKET TALK - Egypt's state wheat buyer said Friday he did not intend to buy wheat this weekend. "We will never buy this weekend. We have lots and lots of wheat," Samir Shakankiri, vice chairman of the state's General Authority for Supply Commodities, told Reuters. He was responding to rumors in international wheat markets that Egypt was about to tender, possibly for 500,000 tonnes.

MARKET TALK - USDA said Armenia has been authorized to buy $15 million worth of wheat under PL 480. The authorization provides for purchase of about 60,000 tonnnes from Jan. 10 to Sept. 30 for delivery Jan. 10 through Dec. 31...USDA said it added wheat to the commodities available to India under the Export Credit Guarantee Program (GSM-102) for fiscal 1997. USDA said the total authorization to India was unchanged at $15 million...USDA reported net export sales during the week ended Dec 26: wheat 359,500 tonnes; corn 447,000; soybeans 293,100; upland cotton 97,000 bales; soymeal 40,800; soyoil 63,900; sorghum 123,800; pima cotton 2,300 and rice 25,600.
